title.en: Machine learning concepts: data, types and generalisation
title.zh: 机器学习的基本概念：数据、属性类型与泛化

description.en: The vocabulary of the subject, the learning settings, how to convert between attribute types and what each choice costs, and why a model is judged on data it has not seen.
description.zh: 这门课的词汇、各种学习设定、属性类型怎么互相转换及每种选择的代价，以及为什么要用没见过的数据来评判模型。

description.en: Coding a nominal attribute as 0, 1, 2, ... and feeding it to a numeric model as if the order and gaps meant something
description.zh: 把名义属性编成 0, 1, 2, ... 当数字喂给数值模型，好像顺序和间隔有意义

description.en: Judging a model by its fit to the training data
description.zh: 用模型对训练数据的拟合程度来评判模型

description.en: Treating discretisation as harmless: the bins throw information away and the cut points are a modelling choice
description.zh: 以为离散化无伤大雅：分箱会丢信息，切点本身就是建模选择

description.en: Assuming every missing value is missing at random
description.zh: 以为所有缺失值都是随机缺失

rows.zh: 我们测过的一个对象：一张图、一次传感器读数、一笔购买

rows.zh: 被测量的一个方面，让我们能比较实例

rows.zh: 一个实例的属性值排在一起

text.en: A training set is $N$ pairs $(\mathbf{x}^{(i)}, y^{(i)})$. Learning means: from these pairs, find a rule that predicts $y$ for a new $\mathbf{x}$ whose label we do not know. The rest of the subject is about which rules, how to find them, and how to tell whether they are any good.
text.zh: 训练集是 $N$ 对 $(\mathbf{x}^{(i)}, y^{(i)})$。学习的意思是：从这些对子里找出一条规则，对一个标签未知的新 $\mathbf{x}$ 预测 $y$。这门课其余的内容，就是在讲有哪些规则、怎么找、怎么判断它们好不好。

title.en: Which kind of learning? Start from the labels
title.zh: 哪一种学习？先看有没有标签

text.en: The first design decision of any project is whether you have labels, and what kind. The deck's concepts are four, and they sort into two families.
text.zh: 任何项目的第一个设计决定，就是有没有标签、是什么标签。讲义里的“概念”有四种，分成两大家族。

rows.en: labelled instances, label is a discrete class
rows.zh: 带标签的实例，标签是离散类别

rows.en: map an instance to its class
Play = yes/no; spam / not spam; digit 0-9
labelled instances, label is a number
rows.zh: 带标签的实例，标签是一个数

rows.en: map an instance to a number
groups of similar students; customer segmentation
rows.zh: 相似的学生群；客户细分
哪些属性值会一起出现

rows.en: milk and bread bought together, so butter is likely too (market basket, "beer and diapers")
rows.zh: 牛奶和面包一起买，黄油也很可能被买（购物篮分析，“啤酒与尿布”）

text.en: **Supervised** learning has prior knowledge of the classes: it learns from labelled data to predict a label or a number for new, unseen instances. **Unsupervised** learning has no inventory of classes: it discovers hidden patterns, groups or relationships in unlabelled data. The deck lists more unsupervised flavours: **anomaly detection** (find instances that do not fit), **dimensionality reduction** (fewer features that keep what matters) and **market basket analysis**.
text.zh: **监督学习**事先知道有哪些类别：用带标签的数据学习，给新的、没见过的实例预测一个标签或一个数。**无监督学习**没有类别清单：在没有标签的数据里发现隐藏的模式、分组或关系。讲义列出的无监督“口味”还有：**异常检测**（找出不合群的实例）、**降维**（用更少的特征保住要紧的信息）和**购物篮分析**。

text.en: Deciding which type to use
text.zh: 怎么决定用哪一类

rows.en: neural network, logistic regression, random forest, naive Bayes, SVM
rows.zh: 神经网络、逻辑回归、随机森林、朴素贝叶斯、SVM

rows.en: SVM, neural network, ridge, random forest, lasso
rows.zh: SVM、神经网络、岭回归、随机森林、lasso
没有：要分组还是要降维？

rows.en: k-means, Gaussian mixture, DBSCAN, spectral, hierarchical
rows.zh: k-means、高斯混合、DBSCAN、谱聚类、层次聚类

text.en: The deck's fuller taxonomy adds two more families. **Semi-supervised** learning has a *few* labels and many unlabelled instances (text classification, lane-finding on GPS data). **Reinforcement** learning has no fixed labelled set: an agent acts, receives rewards, and learns a policy (optimised marketing, driverless cars). Both return in later lessons.
text.zh: 讲义里更完整的分类还多两个家族。**半监督**学习有*少量*标签和大量无标签实例（文本分类、GPS 数据的车道检测）。**强化**学习没有固定的带标签数据集：智能体行动、得到奖励、学出一个策略（营销优化、自动驾驶）。两者在后面的课里还会出现。

body.en: You run a mall with a membership system and hold only customer ID, date of birth and transactions. You do not know income, gender or who the VIPs are. You want to know *who your customers are*. With no labels this is **clustering**: find groups of customers who behave alike, then name them yourself. Success is judged subjectively (are the groups useful for marketing?), so evaluation is the hard part.
body.zh: 你开一家有会员系统的商场，手里只有客户编号、出生日期和交易记录；不知道收入、性别，也不知道谁是 VIP。你想弄清“我的客户是谁”。没有标签，这就是**聚类**：找出行为相似的客户群，再自己给它们起名。好不好只能主观判断（这些群对营销有用吗），所以评估是难点。

prompt.en: A bank has 10,000 past loans, each marked "repaid" or "defaulted", and wants to score new applicants. Which setting?
prompt.zh: 银行有 1 万笔过去的贷款，每笔都标了“已还”或“违约”，想给新的申请人打分。是哪种设定？

label.en: Clustering, because the loans fall into two groups
label.zh: 聚类，因为贷款分成两组

feedback.en: The two groups are given as labels. Clustering is for when nobody tells you the groups.
feedback.zh: 这两组是作为标签给定的。聚类用在没人告诉你分组的时候。

label.en: Classification: labelled data, discrete label
label.zh: 分类：有标签的数据，标签离散

label.en: Regression, because we output a score
label.zh: 回归，因为输出一个分数

feedback.en: The *label* is discrete (repaid/defaulted). A probability score is still a classifier output; regression means the true label is a number.
feedback.zh: *标签*是离散的（已还/违约）。概率分数仍是分类器的输出；回归指的是真实标签本身是个数。

explain.en: Ask two questions: are there labels? are they discrete or numeric?
explain.zh: 问两个问题：有没有标签？标签是离散的还是数值的？

title.en: Classification vs regression, on the weather data
title.zh: 分类与回归，用天气数据看

text.en: Both are supervised and both are scored on **held-out** instances whose labels we know but the model has not seen. The deck splits the 14 weather rows: the first 10 are *training data*, the last 4 *evaluation data*. A classifier trained on the 10 rows predicts Play for the 4:
text.zh: 两者都是监督学习，都在**留出**的实例上打分：我们知道这些实例的标签，模型没见过。讲义把 14 行天气数据分开：前 10 行是*训练数据*，后 4 行是*评估数据*。用前 10 行训练出的分类器，给后 4 行预测 Play：

text.en: A prediction is simply right or wrong: 2 of 4 are right. Regression is different. Here the label is the temperature in degrees and the deck's model predicts the four evaluation rows:
text.zh: 分类的预测非对即错：4 个里对 2 个。回归不同。这里的标签是温度（度数），讲义里的模型对四个评估行的预测是：

text.en: Nobody expects 75.0 exactly; a prediction is 'correct' when it is acceptably close. That is the real difference. In classification we can **enumerate** all possible labels and a prediction must hit the right one. In regression there are infinitely many possible labels, and we ask how far off we were. So the scores differ too: accuracy-style counts for classes, an average of the errors for numbers (here $(6.2+0.8+1.4+7.5)/4 = 3.975$, the mean absolute error, met again in the evaluation lesson).
text.zh: 没人指望正好是 75.0；预测“足够接近”就算对。这才是真正的区别。分类里我们能**列举**所有可能的标签，预测必须命中正确的那一个。回归里可能的标签有无穷多个，我们问的是差了多远。所以打分方式也不同：类别用对错的计数，数值用误差的平均（这里 $(6.2+0.8+1.4+7.5)/4 = 3.975$，即平均绝对误差，评估那一课还会再见）。

prompt.en: Predicting the number of customers tomorrow (0, 1, 2, ...) is…
prompt.zh: 预测明天的客流量（0, 1, 2, ...）属于……

label.en: Classification, because the values are integers we could list
label.zh: 分类，因为取值是整数，可以列出来

feedback.en: The list never ends, and being off by 3 is much better than being off by 300. Closeness matters, so it is regression.
feedback.zh: 这个列表没有尽头，而且差 3 远好过差 300。“接近”有意义，所以是回归。

label.en: Clustering, because customers come in groups
label.zh: 聚类，因为客户分成各种群

feedback.en: We are given the true counts of past days, so it is supervised.
feedback.zh: 过去每天的真实人数是已知的，所以是监督学习。

label.en: Regression: an ordered quantity where being close counts
label.zh: 回归：有序的数量，越接近越好

explain.en: Test: can you list every label, and is a wrong label simply wrong? Then classification. Is "nearly right" meaningful? Then regression.
explain.zh: 判别法：能不能列出所有标签，错了就是错了？那是分类。“差不多对”有意义吗？那是回归。

title.en: Training, evaluation and why they are kept apart
title.zh: 训练数据、评估数据，以及为什么要分开

text.en: A supervised learner is handed **training data** and builds a model from it. We then measure success on **evaluation (held-out) data**: instances whose labels we know, but which the model never saw while learning. In the weather table the split is the horizontal line after row 10.
text.zh: 监督学习算法拿到**训练数据**，从中建出模型。然后我们在**评估（留出）数据**上衡量成功：这些实例的标签我们知道，但学习期间模型从没见过。天气表里，分界线就是第 10 行之后那条横线。

text.en: Why not just score the model on the training rows? Because the model has seen those answers. A model that simply stores the table scores 10 of 10 on them and tells you nothing about a new day. The held-out rows play the role of the future, and the score on them is our estimate of how the model will do in use. This idea, generalisation, is the heart of the last chapter.
text.zh: 为什么不直接在训练行上打分？因为这些答案模型已经见过。一个把表原样存起来的模型，在训练行上 10 题全对，却完全说明不了新的一天会怎样。留出行扮演“未来”，在它们上的得分就是我们对模型实际表现的估计。这个想法就是泛化，最后一章的核心。

prompt.en: You tune a model until its accuracy on the 4 evaluation rows is as high as possible, then report that accuracy. What is wrong?
prompt.zh: 你不停调模型，直到它在 4 个评估行上的准确率最高，然后报告这个准确率。错在哪？

label.en: The evaluation rows were used to make choices, so they no longer stand in for unseen data
label.zh: 评估行被用来做选择了，不再能代表没见过的数据

label.en: Nothing: held-out data is always an honest estimate
label.zh: 没错：留出数据永远是诚实的估计

feedback.en: Only if it was not used for any decision. Tuning on it makes it part of the training process.
feedback.zh: 前提是没用它做过任何决定。拿它来调模型，它就成了训练过程的一部分。

label.en: The accuracy should be reported on the training rows instead
label.zh: 应该报告训练行上的准确率

feedback.en: That is the number that is optimistic by construction.

explain.en: Hold out data that nothing, including your own tuning, has touched. Later lessons give it a name: a validation set for tuning, a test set for the final report.
explain.zh: 留出的数据，任何东西（包括你自己的调参）都不能碰过。后面的课会给它们起名：调参用验证集，最终汇报用测试集。

text.en: What you may *do* with an attribute's values decides which models can use it. There are three kinds; the first two are **discrete**, the last is **continuous**. Class labels have the same three kinds.
text.zh: 你能对一个属性的值*做什么*，决定了哪些模型能用它。属性有三种；前两种是**离散**的，最后一种是**连续**的。类别标签也是这三种。

rows.en: distinct symbols; only names. A two-valued one is a Boolean / dichotomy
rows.zh: 互不相同的符号，只是名字。只有两个值的叫布尔 / 二分

rows.en: an explicit order, but no distance between values
rows.zh: 有明确的顺序，但值之间没有距离

rows.en: real or integer quantities with mathematical meaning
rows.zh: 有数学意义的实数或整数

text.en: Ordinal values rank but do not measure: $\text{hot} - \text{cool} \ne \text{mild}$, because the gaps between levels are unknown. An ordinal rule such as 'temperature < hot → play = yes' is fine; averaging two levels is not. The boundary between nominal and ordinal is sometimes blurred: is outlook {sunny, overcast, rainy} ordered? Decide by whether an order is meaningful for the task.
text.zh: 序数值只排序、不度量：$\text{hot} - \text{cool} \ne \text{mild}$，因为各级之间的间隔未知。“temperature < hot → play = yes”这样的序数规则没问题；把两个等级取平均就不行。名义和序数的界线有时模糊：outlook {sunny, overcast, rainy} 有顺序吗？看这个顺序对任务有没有意义。

prompt.en: Which type is a postcode such as 3010?
prompt.zh: 邮政编码（如 3010）是哪种类型？

label.en: Numeric, it is made of digits
label.zh: 数值，它由数字组成

feedback.en: Subtracting two postcodes means nothing; 3010 is not 3 times 1000. Digits do not make a quantity.
feedback.zh: 两个邮编相减没意义；3010 不是 1000 的 3 倍。写成数字不等于是数量。

label.en: Nominal: a name for a place, only equality is meaningful
label.zh: 名义：一个地方的名字，只有相等有意义

label.en: Ordinal, bigger codes come later
label.zh: 序数，大的邮编排后面

feedback.en: The order of codes is an accident of how they were handed out, not a ranking of anything.
feedback.zh: 邮编的先后只是编号分配的偶然，并不是任何意义上的排名。

explain.en: The deck's quick quiz: blood type (A, B, AB, O) is nominal, movie rating 1★-5★ and T-shirt size XS-XL are ordinal, postcode is nominal.
explain.zh: 讲义的小测验答案：血型（A, B, AB, O）是名义，电影评分 1★-5★ 和 T 恤尺码 XS-XL 是序数，邮编是名义。

title.en: When the attribute and the model do not fit

text.en: Most algorithms assume a certain attribute type. The deck's list:
text.zh: 多数算法默认某种属性类型。讲义的清单：

text.en: If your data has the wrong type (or a mix of types), there are exactly three ways out:
text.zh: 数据类型不对（或各种类型混着），只有三条出路：

items.en: **Select** only the attributes of the right type. Cheap, but you throw information away.
items.zh: **挑选**类型对的属性。便宜，但会丢信息。

items.en: **Change the model's assumptions** to match the data: for example a naive Bayes with a categorical distribution for nominal and a Gaussian for numeric attributes.
items.zh: **改模型的假设**去适应数据：比如朴素贝叶斯对名义属性用类别分布、对数值属性用高斯分布。

items.en: **Change the attributes** to match the model: convert nominal to numeric, or numeric to nominal. The next pages do this.
items.zh: **改属性**去适应模型：名义转数值，或数值转名义。接下来几页就做这件事。

title.zh: 名义转数值：为什么要 one-hot

text.en: The obvious conversion is to number the categories: red, blue, green, orange, pink become 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. It is simple and compact, but it quietly says things that are false.
text.zh: 最顺手的办法是给类别编号：red, blue, green, orange, pink 变成 0, 1, 2, 3, 4。简单又省空间，但它悄悄说了一些假话。

items.en: A **meaningless distance**: pink $-$ red $= 4$, but blue $-$ red $= 1$, as if blue were four times more like red than pink is.
items.zh: **没意义的距离**：pink $-$ red $= 4$，而 blue $-$ red $= 1$，仿佛 blue 比 pink 像 red 四倍。

text.en: **One-hot encoding** gives each category its own 0/1 column and puts a single 1 in the column of the category present:
text.zh: **one-hot 编码**给每个类别一个自己的 0/1 列，只在出现的那个类别的列里放一个 1：

text.en: Now every pair of different colours is exactly the same distance apart, $\sqrt{2}$ (two coordinates differ by 1), so no colour is closer to another than to any other: that is precisely what 'nominal' means. The price, from the deck: the number of features grows with the number of categories (higher dimension), and most entries are 0 (**sparse** data). A 'postcode' attribute with 2,000 values becomes 2,000 columns.
text.zh: 现在任意两种不同的颜色距离完全一样，都是 $\sqrt{2}$（两个坐标各差 1），没有哪个颜色和谁更近：这正是“名义”的含义。代价（讲义指出）：特征数随类别数增长（维度变高），而且大部分取值是 0（**稀疏**）。一个有 2000 个取值的“邮编”属性会变成 2000 列。

text.en: With a bias term, the columns add up to 1 for every row, so one column is redundant (the 'dummy variable trap' of linear regression). Dropping one column ($k-1$ columns for $k$ categories) removes it. An *ordinal* attribute may sensibly be coded 1, 2, 3 when the levels are roughly evenly spaced; that is a judgement, not a rule.
text.zh: 带偏置项时，每一行的各列加起来恒为 1，所以有一列是多余的（线性回归的“虚拟变量陷阱”）。去掉一列（$k$ 个类别用 $k-1$ 列）即可。*序数*属性在各级间隔大致均匀时可以合理地编成 1, 2, 3；这是判断，不是定律。

text.en: **Discretisation** groups numeric values into a fixed set of categories: house prices become {low, medium, high}. Two decisions: how many categories, and where the boundaries go. The deck gives three ways to place boundaries.
text.zh: **离散化**把数值归入固定的几个类别：房价变成 {低, 中, 高}。要做两个决定：分几类，边界放哪。讲义给了三种放边界的办法。

rows.en: find min and max; $n$ bins each of width $(\max-\min)/n$
rows.zh: 找最小最大值；分成 $n$ 个箱，每箱宽 $(\max-\min)/n$

rows.en: unequal data distribution; sensitive to outliers
rows.zh: 数据分布不均；对异常值敏感

rows.en: sort; cut into $n$ bins with the same number of items (use rank order)
rows.zh: 排序；切成 $n$ 个箱，每箱个数相同（按名次）

rows.en: robust to outliers; keeps the data distribution; avoids sparse intervals
rows.zh: 对异常值稳健；保持数据分布；避免稀疏区间

rows.en: loses interpretability; can be inconsistent; information loss
rows.zh: 难解释；可能不一致；信息损失

rows.en: group the values into $n$ clusters, e.g. with k-means
rows.zh: 把值聚成 $n$ 类，例如用 k-means

rows.en: needs $n$ (or a way to choose it); one more model to run
rows.zh: 要给定 $n$（或想办法选）；多跑一个模型

text.en: The deck's equal-width example: education years range from 6 to 18, so with $n=3$ the width is $(18-6)/3 = 4$ and the bins are $[6,10)$, $[10,14)$, $[14,18]$; with $n=2$ the width is 6: $[6,12)$, $[12,18]$. The last bin is closed so the maximum has a home.

alt.en: Nine incomes on a number line, 20 to 200. Equal width: bins hold 8, 0, 1 items. Equal frequency: 3, 3, 3 items.
alt.zh: 数轴上的 9 个收入，20 到 200。等宽：三个箱分别有 8、0、1 个。等频：各 3 个。

say.en: Nine incomes in thousands of dollars: 20, 22, 25, 27, 30, 33, 36, 40, 200. The 200 is an outlier. Equal width needs the extremes.
Bin width is range divided by number of bins.
say.zh: 箱宽 = 极差 / 箱数。

say.en: Add the width to the minimum repeatedly to get the edges.
say.zh: 从最小值起，每次加一个箱宽，得到各边界。

say.en: Count the items per bin. One outlier stretched the range, so eight of nine incomes land in the same bin and the middle bin is empty: the bins describe the outlier, not the data.
say.zh: 数每个箱里有几个。一个异常值撑大了范围，九个收入里八个落进同一个箱，中间箱是空的：这些箱描述的是异常值，不是数据。

say.en: Equal frequency: sort (already sorted) and give each bin the same count.
say.zh: 等频：排序（这里已经排好），每个箱分同样多的个数。

say.en: The bins by rank. The 200 now sits harmlessly with 36 and 40.
say.zh: 按名次分的箱。200 现在安安稳稳地和 36、40 待在一起。

say.en: Put each cut halfway between the last item of one bin and the first of the next: $(25+27)/2$ and $(33+36)/2$. New data are binned with these cuts.
say.zh: 每个切点放在相邻两箱的交界处的中间：$(25+27)/2$ 和 $(33+36)/2$。新数据就按这两个切点分箱。

outro.en: Equal width gave 8 / 0 / 1, equal frequency 3 / 3 / 3. Neither is 'right'; they answer different questions, which the next page looks at.
outro.zh: 等宽得到 8 / 0 / 1，等频得到 3 / 3 / 3。哪个都不是“对”的；它们回答不同的问题，下一页细看。

prompt.en: Width of one equal-width bin for these nine incomes (min 20, max 200, 3 bins).
prompt.zh: 这九个收入的等宽箱宽度（最小 20，最大 200，3 个箱）。

title.en: Deeper: what each discretisation choice costs
title.zh: 深入：每种离散化选择的代价

text.en: Discretisation is not a neutral reformatting. It is a modelling decision, and each part of it has a price.
text.zh: 离散化不是中立的格式转换，而是一个建模决定，每一部分都有代价。

text.en: 1. All information inside a bin is destroyed
text.zh: 1. 箱子里面的信息全部丢掉

text.en: After binning, 33 and 36 become the same value, while 33 and 34.6 (a cut at 34.5) become different values. The model sees a **step**, not a slope: two nearly identical incomes are treated as opposites, and two far apart as equal. Narrow bins lose less, but then each bin has few instances, estimates per bin are noisy, and there are more parameters to learn (overfitting risk). Wide bins are stable but crude. The number of bins is a bias-variance knob in its own right.
text.zh: 分箱之后，33 和 36 变成同一个值，而 33 和 34.6（切点在 34.5）却变成不同的值。模型看到的是**台阶**而不是斜坡：几乎一样的两个收入被当成相反，相差很远的两个被当成相等。箱窄，丢得少，但每箱实例少，每箱的估计噪声大，要学的参数也更多（过拟合风险）。箱宽，稳定但粗糙。箱数本身就是一个偏差-方差旋钮。

text.en: 2. Equal width inherits the shape of the data
text.zh: 2. 等宽继承了数据的形状

text.en: Its boundaries depend only on min and max, so one outlier moves every boundary (8 / 0 / 1 above), and a skewed variable like income leaves the tail bins nearly empty. Its virtue: the bins have a meaning you can state ('\\$20k wide'), and the same cut points can be reused on new data.
text.zh: 它的边界只取决于最小值和最大值，所以一个异常值就会挪动所有边界（上面的 8 / 0 / 1），收入这类偏斜变量会让尾部的箱几乎为空。它的好处：箱有可陈述的含义（“每箱 2 万”），同样的切点可以直接用到新数据上。

text.en: 3. Equal frequency inherits the sample
text.zh: 3. 等频继承了样本

text.en: Its cut points are quantiles of *this* sample, so they are robust to outliers and every bin has enough instances. But a bin may stretch from 36 to 200: the label 'high' covers very different people, and it is hard to say in words what the bin means. If many values are tied, identical values must be split across bins or kept together, making sizes unequal (the 'inconsistency' of the deck). And the cuts must be fitted on the training data only and then applied unchanged to test data; recomputing quantiles on the test set leaks information.
text.zh: 它的切点是*这个*样本的分位数，所以对异常值稳健、每个箱都有足够的实例。但一个箱可能从 36 一直伸到 200：标签“高”涵盖了差别很大的人，也很难用话说清这个箱是什么意思。若有很多相同的值，相同的值要么被劈到不同箱、要么留在一起，箱的大小就不一样了（讲义里的“不一致”）。切点只能用训练数据确定，再原样用到测试数据；在测试集上重算分位数会泄漏信息。

text.en: 4. Clustering, or using the label
text.zh: 4. 聚类，或者利用标签

text.en: Boundaries from clustering follow natural gaps, at the price of another model and a choice of $n$. A supervised variant (choose cuts that best separate the classes, e.g. by information gain) usually loses the least for classification, but it uses the labels, so it must also be fitted on training data only.
text.zh: 聚类得到的边界顺着自然的缺口走，代价是多一个模型、还要选 $n$。监督式的变体（选最能分开类别的切点，比如用信息增益）对分类通常丢得最少，但它用了标签，所以同样只能在训练数据上确定。

prompt.en: Incomes are very skewed (a few billionaires). You discretise into 4 bins and want each bin to be usable by a model. Which is the better default, and what do you give up?
prompt.zh: 收入非常偏斜（有几个亿万富翁）。你把它离散成 4 个箱，希望每个箱模型都能用。哪个是更好的默认选择，代价是什么？

label.en: Equal frequency: every bin has enough data and outliers cannot move the cuts; you give up a simple meaning for each bin
label.zh: 等频：每个箱数据够多，异常值挪不动切点；代价是每个箱不再有简单的含义

label.en: Equal width: bins are easy to state, and sparse bins are harmless
label.zh: 等宽：箱好表述，稀疏的箱也无所谓

feedback.en: Sparse bins are exactly the problem: with a few extreme incomes, most bins hold no data and one holds almost everyone, so the model cannot tell ordinary incomes apart.
feedback.zh: 稀疏的箱恰恰是问题：有几个极端收入，多数箱里没有数据，而一个箱装了几乎所有人，模型分不出普通收入之间的差别。

label.en: Neither: never discretise numeric data
label.zh: 都不要：永远别离散化数值数据

feedback.en: Sometimes you must (a model that needs nominal input), and it can help with non-linear effects. The point is to know the cost, not to ban it.
feedback.zh: 有时必须（模型只吃名义输入），而且它能帮着表达非线性。要点是知道代价，不是一概禁止。

explain.en: The choice depends on what you need: a bin you can state in words (equal width) or bins a model can learn from (equal frequency).
explain.zh: 看你需要什么：能用话讲清的箱（等宽），还是模型学得动的箱（等频）。

title.en: Putting numeric attributes on one scale
title.zh: 把数值属性放到同一个尺度上

say.en: Eight values. Standardisation needs the mean $\mu$ of the attribute.
say.zh: 八个值。标准化先要这个属性的均值 $\mu$。

say.en: and its standard deviation $\sigma$ (the squared distances are 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16, which sum to 32; divided by 8 is 4).
say.zh: 再要标准差 $\sigma$（离差平方依次是 9, 1, 1, 1, 0, 0, 4, 16，和为 32；除以 8 得 4）。

say.en: The z-score says how many standard deviations the value lies from the mean. The result has mean 0 and standard deviation 1, and keeps the shape of the data (an outlier remains an outlier).
say.zh: z 分数表示这个值离均值有几个标准差。结果的均值为 0、标准差为 1，数据的形状不变（异常值仍是异常值）。

say.en: Min-max scaling squeezes the data into exactly $[0,1]$: the minimum goes to 0, the maximum to 1. It is sensitive to a single extreme value, which fixes the whole scale.
say.zh: min-max 缩放把数据压进恰好 $[0,1]$：最小值变 0，最大值变 1。它对单个极端值敏感，因为极端值决定了整个尺度。

intro.en: Why bother? If one attribute is the weight in grams (thousands) and another the price in dollars (tens), any method that adds up differences across attributes (distances in k-NN, gradient steps) is dominated by the big numbers. Rescaling lets each attribute count fairly. Take the eight values 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9.
intro.zh: 为什么要缩放？如果一个属性是以克计的重量（上千），另一个是以美元计的价格（几十），任何把各属性的差异加起来的方法（k-NN 的距离、梯度步长）都会被大数字主导。重新缩放让每个属性公平地算数。取八个值 2, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 7, 9。

outro.en: Fit $\mu,\sigma$ (or min, max) on the training data and reuse them on the test data, never recompute them there.
outro.zh: $\mu,\sigma$（或最小、最大值）在训练数据上确定，在测试数据上沿用，不要在那里重算。

title.en: Real data is messy: missing values

text.en: Data comes from several departments with different conventions, periods and errors, and must be assembled and cleaned before any model sees it. The biggest issue is **missing values**: unknown, unrecorded or irrelevant entries, caused by broken equipment, changes in experimental design or merged datasets.
text.zh: 数据来自几个部门，约定、时间段、错误各不相同，在任何模型看到之前都要先拼起来、清理干净。最大的问题是**缺失值**：未知、没记录或不相关的条目，原因可能是设备故障、实验设计改变、数据集合并。

rows.en: the chance a value is missing is unrelated to any measured variable and to the missing value itself; no rule predicts what is missing
rows.zh: 值缺失的概率与任何已测变量和缺失值本身无关；没有规则能预测缺了什么

rows.en: most algorithms assume this; simple imputation is acceptable
rows.zh: 多数算法都假定这一点；简单填补尚可接受

rows.en: missingness depends on the value itself (even after controlling for other variables): a rule can predict what is missing
rows.zh: 缺失取决于值本身（即使控制了其他变量）：有规则能预测缺了什么

rows.en: the fact that it is missing carries information (a medical test not ordered); filling it in hides this
rows.zh: “缺失”这件事本身带有信息（没开的医学检查）；填上就把信息抹掉了

text.en: **Disguised missing data** is a missing value that was filled with a default: everyone born on 1 January, every email xx@xx.com. Look for suspicious values using domain knowledge. **Inaccurate data** (typos, sensor faults, outliers) must be found the same way.
text.zh: **伪装的缺失数据**是用默认值填上的缺失：所有人都生于 1 月 1 日，所有邮箱都是 xx@xx.com。要靠领域知识找可疑的值。**不准确的数据**（笔误、传感器故障、异常值）也要这样找出来。

text.en: **Simple imputation** fills a gap with the mean, median or mode of the attribute. It is easy and keeps every record. Its cost, which the deck names: it biases other statistics. Observed values [2, 4, 8, 10] have mean 6 and variance 10. Fill a missing fifth value with the mean 6 and the variance falls to 8: the filled-in point sits exactly in the middle and adds no spread, so the data look less variable than they are. The median is more robust to outliers; the mode is for nominal attributes.
text.zh: **简单填补**用该属性的均值、中位数或众数填上缺口。简单，且保留了每条记录。它的代价（讲义点明）：会扭曲其他统计量。已观测的值 [2, 4, 8, 10] 均值 6、方差 10。把缺失的第五个值填成均值 6，方差就掉到 8：填进去的点正落在中间，不增加任何离散度，数据看上去比实际更集中。中位数对异常值更稳健；众数用于名义属性。

text.en: Finally, **get to know the data**: histograms for nominal attributes (does the distribution match what you know?), scatter plots for numeric attributes (any obvious outliers?), 2-D and 3-D plots for dependencies, domain experts for what the values mean, and a sample if there is too much to inspect.
text.zh: 最后，**了解你的数据**：名义属性看直方图（分布和你的认知一致吗？），数值属性看散点图（有明显的异常值吗？），2 维、3 维图看依赖关系，问领域专家这些值的含义，数据太多就取样看。

prompt.en: In a clinic dataset, "blood glucose" is missing for patients the doctor judged healthy. Which is it, and what follows?
prompt.zh: 在一份诊所数据里，医生认为健康的病人没有测“血糖”。这是哪种缺失，会怎样？

label.en: Disguised missing data, since glucose is a default
label.zh: 伪装的缺失，因为血糖是个默认值

feedback.en: Disguised missing data has a fake value filled in. Here the field is simply empty.
feedback.zh: 伪装的缺失是被填上了假值。这里字段只是空着。

label.en: MAR: some values are always lost
label.zh: MAR：总有些值会丢

feedback.en: Under MAR the chance of a gap is unrelated to the patient's state. Here a rule (the doctor's judgement) predicts the gap.
feedback.zh: MAR 下出现缺口的概率与病人状况无关。这里有一条规则（医生的判断）能预测缺口。

label.en: MNAR: missingness depends on the patient's condition, so "missing" itself is informative; filling with the mean would hide that
label.zh: MNAR：缺失取决于病人的状况，“缺失”本身就有信息；用均值填就把这一点藏起来了

explain.en: Add an indicator attribute "was measured" so the model can use the missingness as a feature.
explain.zh: 再加一个“是否测过”的指示属性，让模型把缺失当成一个特征来用。

title.en: Deeper: what a model is, and what learning does
title.zh: 深入：模型是什么，学习做了什么

text.en: A **model** is a function $f$ that maps an instance's features to a prediction, $\hat{y} = f(\mathbf{x})$. **Learning** (training) is choosing $f$ from a family of candidate functions, the **hypothesis space**, using the training data. A k-NN, a decision tree and a logistic regression are three different families; inside a family, the parameters ($\boldsymbol\theta$, tree splits) are what training sets.
text.zh: **模型**是一个函数 $f$，把实例的特征映射成预测 $\hat{y} = f(\mathbf{x})$。**学习**（训练）就是用训练数据，从一族候选函数，即**假设空间**里挑出 $f$。k-NN、决策树、逻辑回归是三个不同的函数族；在一个函数族里，训练要定的是参数（$\boldsymbol\theta$、树的分裂）。

text.en: What should 'a good $f$' mean? There is one trivial answer: a lookup table that stores every training row has zero error on the training data. On the weather table it scores 10/10, and it has no idea what to say about a rainy, cool, high-humidity day it has not stored. It has **memorised**, not learned. The same happens with curves:
text.zh: “好的 $f$”该是什么意思？有一个平凡的答案：把每个训练行都存下来的查找表，在训练数据上误差为零。在天气表上它 10 题全对，却完全不知道没存过的“雨天、凉、湿度高”该说什么。它是**背下来**了，不是学会了。曲线也一样：

alt.en: Seven noisy points. A straight line follows the trend; a degree-6 curve passes through every point but swings wildly between them.
alt.zh: 七个带噪声的点。直线跟随趋势；6 次曲线穿过每个点，但在点与点之间剧烈摆动。

caption.en: The wiggly curve has zero training error, and it would predict badly between and beyond the points.
caption.zh: 弯弯曲曲的曲线训练误差为零，但在点与点之间和点以外预测得很差。

title.en: Deeper: why generalisation, not training fit, is the goal
title.zh: 深入：为什么目标是泛化，而不是拟合训练数据

text.en: We assume the data are **independent and identically distributed (i.i.d.)** draws from some unknown distribution $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$, and the future instances come from the same one. The thing we truly care about is the **generalisation error**: the expected loss of $f$ on a *fresh* draw,
text.zh: 我们假定数据是从某个未知分布 $P(\mathbf{x}, y)$ **独立同分布（i.i.d.）**抽出来的，未来的实例也来自同一个分布。我们真正在意的是**泛化误差**：$f$ 在一次*新*抽样上的期望损失，

text.en: where $\ell$ is the loss (0 for a right class and 1 for a wrong one, or squared error). $R(f)$ cannot be computed, because $P$ is unknown. What we can compute is the **training error**, the average of $\ell$ over the training rows. It is an *optimistic* estimate of $R(f)$, because $f$ was chosen precisely so that this number is small: the more flexible the family, the better it can be fitted to the noise in these particular rows, and the wider the gap between the two numbers.
text.zh: 其中 $\ell$ 是损失（分类对为 0、错为 1，或平方误差）。$R(f)$ 算不出来，因为 $P$ 未知。能算的是**训练误差**，即训练行上 $\ell$ 的平均。它是 $R(f)$ 的一个*过于乐观*的估计，因为 $f$ 正是为了让这个数小而选出来的：函数族越灵活，越能贴合这几行里的噪声，两个数之间的差距就越大。

text.en: That is why held-out data is used: rows that took no part in choosing $f$ are an honest sample from $P$, so their average loss is an unbiased estimate of $R(f)$. Compare the two failure modes:
text.zh: 这就是为什么要用留出数据：没参与挑选 $f$ 的行是从 $P$ 里诚实抽出的样本，它们上的平均损失是 $R(f)$ 的无偏估计。比较两种失败：

rows.en: too simple (straight line through a curve)
rows.zh: 太简单（用直线去拟合曲线）
太灵活（把噪声也存下来）

text.en: Choosing a model because its *training* error is smallest therefore always picks the most flexible one. Models are chosen by held-out performance, and the goal is the best $R(f)$ you can get from a finite sample.
text.zh: 所以，若按*训练*误差最小来选模型，永远会选中最灵活的那个。选模型要看留出数据上的表现，目标是在有限样本下得到尽可能好的 $R(f)$。

prompt.en: A model has 100% accuracy on the training data and 60% on held-out data. Which statement is the best reading?
prompt.zh: 一个模型在训练数据上准确率 100%，在留出数据上 60%。哪种解读最好？

label.en: It is excellent, since it is perfect on the data it knows
label.zh: 它很出色，因为在已知数据上完美

feedback.en: Perfect on known data is cheap (a lookup table does it). What counts is the unseen data: 60%.
feedback.zh: 在已知数据上完美很容易（查找表就行）。要紧的是没见过的数据：60%。

label.en: It is overfitted: it fits the training rows, noise included, but does not generalise
label.zh: 过拟合：它把训练行连同噪声都拟合了，但不能泛化

label.en: Underfitted: the model is too simple
label.zh: 欠拟合：模型太简单

feedback.en: An underfitted model is also poor on the *training* data. Here training is perfect and the gap is the signal.
feedback.zh: 欠拟合的模型在*训练*数据上也不好。这里训练数据上是完美的，差距才是信号。

explain.en: A large gap between training and held-out performance is the signature of overfitting.
explain.zh: 训练和留出表现之间差距很大，就是过拟合的标志。

title.en: Deeper: why learning needs an assumption, by counting functions
title.zh: 深入：数一数函数，看学习为什么必须有假设

say.en: Take $3$ yes/no attributes. Each attribute doubles the number of distinct instances, so there are 8 possible instances in total.
say.zh: 取 $3$ 个是/否属性。每个属性让不同实例的数目翻倍，所以一共有 8 种可能的实例。

say.en: A rule gives each of the 8 instances a label yes or no, independently. That makes $2^8$ possible rules (Boolean functions). This is the hypothesis space if we allow *any* rule.
say.zh: 一条规则给 8 个实例各自独立地打上 yes 或 no。所以有 $2^8$ 条可能的规则（布尔函数）。若不加任何限制，这就是假设空间。

say.en: Five training rows fix five of the labels. The rules that agree with all five are those that label the remaining three instances freely: $2^3 = 8$ of them, and they disagree with each other on those three.
say.zh: 五个训练行固定了五个标签。与这五个都吻合的规则，就是对剩下三个实例随便打标签的那些：$2^3 = 8$ 条，它们在这三个实例上互相矛盾。

say.en: With 10 attributes there are 1024 instances and about $10^{308}$ rules. No dataset you will ever have covers more than a sliver of the instance space.
say.zh: 10 个属性时有 1024 个实例，约 $10^{308}$ 条规则。你能拿到的任何数据集都只覆盖实例空间的一小条。

say.en: So the data alone can never say what to predict on an unseen instance. Something else must pick one rule among the many that fit: this extra something is the **inductive bias**.
say.zh: 所以，仅凭数据永远说不出对没见过的实例该预测什么。必须有别的东西在所有吻合的规则里挑一条：这个“别的东西”就是**归纳偏置**。

intro.en: Why must a learner assume something? Count the possible rules for a tiny problem.
intro.zh: 为什么学习算法必须假设点什么？数一数一个很小的问题里有多少条可能的规则。

outro.en: This is a version of the 'no free lunch' idea: averaged over all possible problems, no learner beats any other. A learner is good only on problems whose structure matches its bias.
outro.zh: 这是“没有免费午餐”思想的一个版本：在所有可能的问题上取平均，没有哪种学习算法能胜过别的。一个学习算法只在结构和它的偏置相配的问题上才好用。

title.en: Deeper: inductive bias, the bet every model makes
title.zh: 深入：归纳偏置，每个模型下的注

text.en: **Inductive bias** is the set of assumptions a learner uses to prefer one hypothesis over the others that fit the data equally well. It comes in two forms: a **restriction bias** limits the hypothesis space (only straight lines, only trees of depth 3); a **preference bias** allows many hypotheses but ranks them (choose the smallest tree that fits, the smallest weights, the shortest description).
text.zh: **归纳偏置**是学习算法用来在同样吻合数据的多个假设中偏爱其一的那套假设。有两种形式：**限制偏置**缩小假设空间（只许直线、只许深度 3 的树）；**偏好偏置**允许很多假设但给它们排序（选吻合数据的最小的树、最小的权重、最短的描述）。

text.en: The methods of this subject are, in this light, different bets about what a good rule looks like:
text.zh: 从这个角度看，这门课的各种方法，就是对“好规则长什么样”下的不同赌注：

head.zh: 什么时候好 / 什么时候差

rows.en: close instances have the same label
classes form compact regions / irrelevant or badly scaled attributes ruin "close"
rows.zh: 类别形成紧凑的区域 / 无关或尺度不一的属性会毁掉“靠近”

rows.en: the label depends on a few attributes, through axis-aligned yes/no tests; prefer small trees
rows.zh: 标签只由少数几个属性，经轴对齐的是/否检验决定；偏好小树

rows.en: rule-like data / diagonal boundaries need many splits
rows.zh: 规则式的数据 / 斜的边界要很多次分裂

rows.en: attributes are independent given the class
rows.zh: 给定类别后各属性相互独立

rows.en: many weak, unrelated clues, e.g. words / strongly correlated attributes get counted twice
rows.zh: 很多弱而不相关的线索，如单词 / 强相关的属性会被重复计数
线性 / 逻辑回归、感知机

rows.en: the label changes smoothly and additively with the attributes; a straight boundary
rows.zh: 标签随属性平滑、可加地变化；边界是直的
大致线性的数据 / 类似 XOR 的数据

text.en: A model with a **strong** bias (few hypotheses) cannot fit much, so it may *underfit*, but needs little data to pick one. A model with a **weak** bias (many hypotheses) can fit almost anything, so it may *overfit*, and needs much more data. Choosing a model is choosing a bias that matches your problem; there is no bias that is right for all of them. This is the thread behind the bias-variance lesson later.
text.zh: **强**偏置（假设很少）的模型拟合不了多少东西，可能*欠拟合*，但只要很少数据就能选定一个。**弱**偏置（假设很多）的模型几乎什么都能拟合，可能*过拟合*，需要多得多的数据。选模型就是选一个与你的问题相配的偏置；没有一种偏置对所有问题都对。这条线索会在后面的偏差-方差一课里接上。

prompt.en: Ages of nine customers: 21, 23, 24, 25, 29, 31, 34, 38, 60. Discretise into 3 equal-width bins. How many customers fall in the first bin? (The last bin is closed on the right.)
prompt.zh: 九位客户的年龄：21, 23, 24, 25, 29, 31, 34, 38, 60。离散成 3 个等宽的箱。第一个箱里有几位客户？（最后一个箱右端闭合。）

explain.en: Width $= (60-21)/3 = 13$, so the bins are $[21,34)$, $[34,47)$, $[47,60]$. Ages below 34: 21, 23, 24, 25, 29, 31, which is 6. (The 60 stretches the range: bin 2 holds only 34 and 38, bin 3 only 60.)

prompt.en: An attribute has values 4, 6, 6, 8, 8, 10, 12, 14. Standardise the value 14 (use the population standard deviation, dividing by 8). Give the z-score to 2 decimals.
prompt.zh: 某属性的取值是 4, 6, 6, 8, 8, 10, 12, 14。把值 14 标准化（用总体标准差，即除以 8）。答案取两位小数。

prompt.en: A k-NN classifier measures Euclidean distance between instances. One attribute is shirt colour {red, green, blue}. How should it be given to the model?
prompt.zh: k-NN 分类器用欧氏距离衡量实例之间的远近。其中一个属性是衬衫颜色 {red, green, blue}。该怎么交给模型？

label.en: Code red = 0, green = 1, blue = 2 in one column
label.zh: 一列里编码 red = 0, green = 1, blue = 2

feedback.en: Then red is closer to green than to blue, a distance that exists only because of the numbering.
feedback.zh: 这样 red 离 green 比离 blue 近，这个距离只是编号编出来的。

label.en: One-hot: three 0/1 columns, so all different colours are equally far apart
label.zh: one-hot：三个 0/1 列，所有不同的颜色距离相等

label.en: Drop the attribute, because a distance cannot use a nominal attribute
label.zh: 丢掉这个属性，因为距离用不了名义属性

feedback.en: Dropping is allowed (one of the three options) but loses information; one-hot keeps it.
feedback.zh: 丢掉是允许的（三条出路之一），但会丢信息；one-hot 能保住它。

explain.en: Integer codes invent an order and distances; one-hot keeps nominal values equally far apart, at the cost of more columns.
explain.zh: 整数编码凭空造出顺序和距离；one-hot 让名义值彼此等距，代价是列数变多。

prompt.en: In a survey, high earners are far more likely to leave "income" blank. A colleague fills the blanks with the mean income. What is the main problem?
prompt.zh: 在一次调查里，高收入者更常把“收入”留空。同事用平均收入填空。主要问题是什么？

label.en: The data are MNAR, so the mean is too low and "blank" is itself informative
label.zh: 数据是 MNAR，所以均值偏低，而且“留空”本身有信息

label.en: Mean imputation changes the data type to nominal
label.zh: 均值填补会把数据类型变成名义

feedback.en: The type stays numeric. The issue is the bias, not the type.
feedback.zh: 类型仍是数值。问题在偏差，不在类型。

label.en: The data are MAR, so the mean is unbiased but the variance is too large
label.zh: 数据是 MAR，所以均值无偏、方差偏大

feedback.en: Not MAR: the chance of a gap depends on the value. And imputation shrinks the variance, it does not enlarge it.
feedback.zh: 不是 MAR：缺口的概率取决于值本身。而且填补会让方差变小，不会变大。

explain.en: When missingness depends on the value, filling with the mean of the observed values is biased low here, and the model loses the signal that blank means high.
explain.zh: 当缺失取决于值本身，用已观测值的均值去填，在这里会偏低，模型也丢了“空白意味着高”这个信号。

prompt.en: Compare equal-width and equal-frequency discretisation: give one advantage and one disadvantage of each. (Section A style, 3-4 lines.)
prompt.zh: 比较等宽和等频离散化：各给出一个优点和一个缺点。（A 部分风格，3-4 行。）

key_points.en: Equal width: simple and interpretable bins
Equal width: sensitive to outliers / unequal counts per bin
key_points.zh: 等宽：对异常值敏感 / 各箱个数不均

key_points.en: Equal frequency: robust to outliers, similar counts per bin
key_points.zh: 等频：对异常值稳健，各箱个数相近

key_points.en: Equal frequency: bins hard to interpret, information loss / ties make it inconsistent
key_points.zh: 等频：箱难解释、信息损失 / 相同值使其不一致

model_answer.en: Equal width splits the range [min, max] into n bins of the same width. It is simple and the bins are easy to interpret, but one outlier stretches the range, so most data can fall in one bin. Equal frequency puts the same number of instances in each bin, so it is robust to outliers and every bin has data, but the bin widths vary, so a bin is hard to describe, and detail inside a bin is lost.
model_answer.zh: Equal width splits the range [min, max] into n bins of the same width. It is simple and the bins are easy to interpret, but one outlier stretches the range, so most data can fall in one bin. Equal frequency puts the same number of instances in each bin, so it is robust to outliers and every bin has data, but the bin widths vary, so a bin is hard to describe, and detail inside a bin is lost.

explain.en: Name the property each method is built on (the range, the count) and follow it to its consequence.
explain.zh: 指出每种方法依据的是什么（范围、个数），再顺着推出后果。

prompt.en: A model has 98% accuracy on its training data. Explain in 2-3 lines why this does not tell us how it will perform in use, and what we do instead.
prompt.zh: 一个模型在训练数据上准确率为 98%。用 2-3 行解释为什么这说明不了它实际使用时的表现，以及应该怎么做。

key_points.en: Training data was used to fit the model, so training accuracy is optimistic
key_points.zh: 训练数据参与了拟合，训练准确率偏乐观

key_points.en: Overfitting / memorising noise does not generalise
key_points.zh: 过拟合 / 记住噪声不能泛化

key_points.en: Evaluate on held-out data the model has not seen
key_points.zh: 在模型没见过的留出数据上评估

model_answer.en: The model was fitted to the training data, so its accuracy there is optimistic: a flexible model can memorise the noise and still fail on new data (overfitting). What we care about is generalisation, so we measure accuracy on held-out data that was not used in training or tuning, which stands in for unseen data.
model_answer.zh: The model was fitted to the training data, so its accuracy there is optimistic: a flexible model can memorise the noise and still fail on new data (overfitting). What we care about is generalisation, so we measure accuracy on held-out data that was not used in training or tuning, which stands in for unseen data.

explain.en: Three points: optimistic, overfitting, held-out data.
explain.zh: 三个要点：乐观、过拟合、留出数据。

prompt.en: A mall wants to understand its members from customer ID, date of birth and transaction history, with no other information. Propose an approach: which learning setting, which attributes you would build and how you would prepare them, and how you would judge success. (Section C style, about a third of a page.)
prompt.zh: 商场想只凭客户编号、出生日期和交易记录来了解会员，没有其他信息。提出一个方案：用哪种学习设定，构造哪些属性、怎样预处理，怎样判断成功。（C 部分风格，约三分之一页。）

key_points.zh: 无监督：对客户聚类（没有标签）

key_points.en: Attributes from the data: age from date of birth, spend, frequency, recency; numeric, so scale them (standardise)
key_points.zh: 从数据构造属性：由出生日期得年龄、消费额、频率、最近一次消费；数值型，需缩放（标准化）

key_points.en: Handle missing or suspicious values (disguised missing, e.g. default birthdays)
key_points.zh: 处理缺失或可疑的值（伪装的缺失，如默认生日）

key_points.en: Evaluation is subjective: inspect and name clusters, check they are useful for marketing
key_points.zh: 评估是主观的：查看并命名各群，检查对营销是否有用

model_answer.en: This is an unsupervised problem: there are no labels, so I would cluster customers (for example with k-means or hierarchical clustering). From the raw data I would build numeric attributes per customer: age (from the date of birth), total spend, number of visits and days since the last visit. Because the attributes have very different scales, I would standardise them (z-score) so that no attribute dominates the distance. I would check for disguised missing data such as many members born on 1 January, and decide how to impute or drop them. Success cannot be measured against labels, so I would examine each cluster's profile, give it a meaning (such as frequent low spenders) and judge whether it supports different marketing actions, perhaps also checking that clusters are stable across runs.
model_answer.zh: This is an unsupervised problem: there are no labels, so I would cluster customers (for example with k-means or hierarchical clustering). From the raw data I would build numeric attributes per customer: age (from the date of birth), total spend, number of visits and days since the last visit. Because the attributes have very different scales, I would standardise them (z-score) so that no attribute dominates the distance. I would check for disguised missing data such as many members born on 1 January, and decide how to impute or drop them. Success cannot be measured against labels, so I would examine each cluster's profile, give it a meaning (such as frequent low spenders) and judge whether it supports different marketing actions, perhaps also checking that clusters are stable across runs.

explain.en: A design answer: setting, attributes with preparation, and evaluation, each justified in one sentence.
explain.zh: 设计题的答法：设定、属性及其预处理、评估，每一项用一句话说明理由。

rows.en: instance = row, attribute/feature = column, concept = the label to learn; feature vector $\mathbf{x}$
rows.zh: 实例 = 行，属性/特征 = 列，概念 = 要学的标签；特征向量 $\mathbf{x}$

rows.en: supervised: classification (discrete label), regression (numeric label); unsupervised: clustering, association, anomaly detection, dimensionality reduction
rows.zh: 监督：分类（离散标签）、回归（数值标签）；无监督：聚类、关联、异常检测、降维

rows.en: can all labels be listed (right or wrong) vs infinitely many (close enough)
rows.zh: 标签能否全部列出（对或错） vs 有无穷多（够接近就行）

rows.en: nominal: =; ordinal: = and order, no distances; numeric: all arithmetic
rows.zh: 名义：=；序数：= 和顺序，无距离；数值：所有算术

rows.en: integer codes invent order and distance; one-hot is fair but adds columns and sparsity
rows.zh: 整数编码凭空造出顺序和距离；one-hot 公平，但增加列数和稀疏性

rows.en: equal width: $(\max-\min)/n$, simple, outlier-sensitive; equal frequency: same count, robust, hard to interpret; clustering
rows.zh: 等宽：$(\max-\min)/n$，简单，怕异常值；等频：个数相同，稳健，难解释；聚类

rows.en: z-score $(x-\mu)/\sigma$; min-max $(x-\min)/(\max-\min)$; fit on training data
rows.zh: z 分数 $(x-\mu)/\sigma$；min-max $(x-\min)/(\max-\min)$；在训练数据上确定

rows.en: MAR vs MNAR, disguised missing; mean/median/mode imputation shrinks variance
rows.zh: MAR vs MNAR，伪装的缺失；均值/中位数/众数填补会让方差变小

rows.en: goal = error on unseen data; training error is optimistic; evaluate on held-out data
rows.zh: 目标 = 没见过的数据上的误差；训练误差偏乐观；在留出数据上评估

rows.en: data alone never fixes the rule; each model bets on a structure; strong bias underfits, weak bias overfits
rows.zh: 光靠数据定不下规则；每个模型都押注一种结构；偏置强则欠拟合，偏置弱则过拟合
